end.summary:
Zoya defined colonial rule and explained the Company’s early trading role.
They sequenced the Company’s charter (1600), Plassey (1757), Buxar (1764), Diwani rights (1765), and Crown rule (1858).
They explained how forts, armies, battles, alliances, and revenue rights supported the Company’s expansion.
They described Diwani rights as permission to collect revenue and linked local revenue to trade and army costs.
They explained the effects of machine-made cloth on Bengal’s weavers and towns.
end.parentNote: Zoya practised how the East India Company changed from a trading company into a ruling power. They used dates and key events to build the sequence, and clearly explained why Diwani rights strengthened the Company’s finances. One point about who helped remove Siraj-ud-Daulah was uncertain and was not clearly corrected later; reviewing the Plassey–Mir Jafar relationship at home would help. You could ask Zoya to retell the sequence using five date cards.
